note: Self-review checklist for the clinical reviewer (plan §10, §14). 'self' is the author's self-review, not clinical sign-off; every item awaits clinical review. Evidence paths are relative to the repository root.

items.statement: The gland lies in front of and below the ear, over the posterior masseter, wrapping behind the ramus, in front of the sternocleidomastoid.
items.reference: Source CT with TotalSegmentator masks; Visible Human cryosections a_vm1160/1175/1190; standard atlas lateral view

self.note: Segmented from the donor CT; lateral boundary matches the photographed gland edge within about 3 mm.

items.statement: Superficial and deep 'lobes' are defined by the facial-nerve plane (a surgical construct, not true lobes).
items.reference: Pujol-Olmo 2020 (61-69% superficial by weight, 19 specimens)

self.note: 59% superficial in this model (reported, not tuned); the plane is a smooth surface through the authored nerve.

items.statement: The retromandibular (deep) portion is authored within anatomical bounds because the CT does not resolve it; muscle-density tissue beside the posterior digastric is excluded.
items.reference: CT density; cryosection a_vm1175

self.note: Authored region (7.7 mL); the stylomandibular-tunnel extension is not modelled; the cryosection overlay still suggests about 3 mm overlap with muscle at z 231, within registration uncertainty.

items.statement: The trunk leaves the stylomastoid foramen, runs about 1.5 cm, enters the gland, divides at the pes and fans into five branch groups.
items.reference: Cited trunk-length range 8.6-22.8 mm; landmark picks on CT

self.note: Trunk 17.2 mm. One common pattern without interconnections; not verified against cryosections (the nerve is not resolvable at 0.33 mm/px).

items.statement: Within the gland the nerve lies lateral (superficial) to the retromandibular vein; the external carotid lies deep to the vein.
items.reference: Relationship checks on CT; cryosection overlays at three levels

self.note: Relationships hold; the authored vessels lie 1-5 mm from the photographed vessels, within registration uncertainty.

items.statement: Tympanomastoid suture, posterior belly of the digastric, tragal pointer and styloid relate to the trunk as described.
items.reference: Witt 2005, Rea 2010, Pather 2006, Cannon 2004 (measured distances disagree)

self.note: The tragal-pointer distance (19.7 mm) is outside both study ranges; the claim is marked uncertain and the distance is reported, not asserted.

items.statement: The great auricular nerve ascends over the sternocleidomastoid toward the lobule, dividing near the lower pole of the gland.
items.reference: StatPearls; relationship to the SCM surface

self.note: Authored from the spec on the SCM surface; not traced on cryosections.

items.statement: A 2 cm pleomorphic adenoma in the superficial lobe, clear of the nerve.
items.reference: Authored for teaching (size and position), not taken from imaging

self.note: 19 mm, entirely lateral to the nerve plane, 1.6 mm from the nearest branch; the skin fullness over it is authored (up to 2.2 mm).

items.statement: Skin, subcutaneous fat, SMAS and the gland capsule, in that order from outside.
items.reference: Depth bands under the fitted skin

self.note: Layers are constant-depth bands (fat to 7 mm, SMAS 1.3 mm, capsule 1 mm), not segmented; the capsule is thin because the gland lies 3.9 mm under the skin at the lower pole in the source CT.

items.statement: A modified Blair incision: preauricular crease, around the lobule, into a neck crease below the angle.
items.reference: Iowa protocol; StatPearls (representative technique)

self.note: Representative, not universal; the facelift variant is out of M1 scope.

items.statement: The skin flap is raised superficial to the parotid fascia and held forward.
items.reference: Iowa protocol; StatPearls

self.note: Skin and fat fold forward as one curl; the neck part is subplatysmal in practice but there is no platysma mesh, so the operative plates hide the SMAS outside the capsule.

items.statement: Antegrade dissection lifts the superficial lobe off the nerve branches with the tumour inside it.
items.reference: Representative superficial parotidectomy

self.note: The peel is a fold driven by an antegrade order field; it shows the principle, not tissue mechanics.

items.statement: The face is generic (MPFB, CC0), not the donor's.
items.reference: Face fit report

self.note: Conformed to the CT only over the dissection field; the central face is unconformed MPFB.

items.statement: The gland is divided into the five ESGS levels (I-IV of the body and the accessory lobule) with the extracapsular cuff around the tumour, and each operation takes the pieces its definition names.
items.reference: Quer 2016 (ESGS classification; full text unavailable); Pujol-Olmo 2020 level weights; Zanghì 2024 definitions

self.note: Level boundaries follow the nerve plane and a surface through the buccal branch, so the level shares (I 8%, II 51%, III 30%, IV 10%) differ from the published ones. Reported, not tuned.

items.statement: Branching patterns follow the Katz-Catalano types with their pooled prevalence, drawn on the same model.
items.reference: Katz and Catalano 1987; Triantafyllou 2024

self.note: The interconnecting twigs are schematic in position: the sources give patterns and prevalence, not coordinates. The default pattern has no interconnections.

items.statement: A pleomorphic adenoma can lie in the outer lobe, the inner lobe, the tail or the accessory lobule.
items.reference: Placement checks (clear of nerve, vessels, bone, muscle)

self.note: Alternate placements are authored for teaching; sizes and positions are not taken from imaging.

items.statement: Imaging is represented by the donor's normal CT slice with the tumour drawn as an outline, an ultrasound probe with its imaging plane as an outline, and a needle; no scan of a tumour is shown.
items.reference: Lee 2008; Martino 2020; Brennan 2012; Christe 2011; Liu 2016; Wang 2022; Kim 2018

self.note: The abstracts give rates and roles, not technique; the instruments are placed for illustration. No ultrasound or MRI picture is drawn.

items.statement: Closure options (SMAS flap, neck-muscle strip, graft sheet), a drain through a separate neck exit, and layered skin closure.
items.reference: De Virgilio 2021; Dulguerov 2016; Ye 2019; Iowa protocol

self.note: The SMAS sheet is a hinged fold that does not drape onto the bed; the strip is a rigid turn; the graft is a plain sheet. The evidence compares options only indirectly and is of low certainty; the plates do not recommend one.

items.statement: What is removed and what remains, the contour change, the specimen opened on the bench, and one hospital's routine day by day.
items.reference: Lambiel 2021; Bovenzi 2019; Zbaren and Stauffer 2007; Iowa protocol

self.note: The hollow is drawn at an illustrative depth; the healing timeline is one institution's practice, not evidence; the specimen is a model of the pieces taken, not a section of a real tumour.

items.statement: Each complication is mapped to the structure responsible and to the skin where it is felt, with every rate shown with its population.
items.reference: Jin 2019; Bron and O'Brien 1997; Mortensen 2024; Lambiel 2021; Choi 2013; Linkov 2012; Lammek 2021; Britt 2017; Dulguerov 2017; Hintze 2021

self.note: Territories are ellipsoids, not measured boundaries; Frey regrowth, the saliva collection and the returning nodules are schematic. Rates differ several-fold between series and are shown, not reconciled.

items.statement: The viewer can handle the model: a depth dial per tissue family, orbit and zoom, structure cards, and the four resections carried out step by step; the comparison shows what each takes from the same gland.
items.reference: The model's own pieces (frame.json)

self.note: The facelift incision is a planned line only (the flap is cut along the Blair path). Volumes are properties of this one gland.
